text:
ash_product: thanks for the candid Qs in today's all-hands. reopening the thread for quick clarifications on mission & positioning. keep it short please :slightly_smiling_face:

marc_sales: when a buyer says 'we care about latency and cost', what's the two-sentence response?

leila_ceo: say: we optimize inference so latency is predictable and per-token cost is controllable. we give teams concrete knobs (batching, cache, quantization) and deployment choices (hosted/dedicated/private) to tune that tradeoff.

vish_engineer: follow-up: what counts as "predictable"? any concrete metric we can cite?

leila_ceo: predictable = SLO-driven percentiles. e.g., we target 99th-percentile latency SLAs on Dedicated and give per-route dashboards showing variance and cost breakdowns. numbers differ by model & workload, so point them to our perf pages for examples.

anya_research: competitor nuance: how to phrase the difference vs model-hosting marketplaces that just list endpoints?

marc_sales: short: marketplaces give model access; we give serving economics + ops controls. we actually manage runtime, fallbacks, and tooling so teams ship features not infra.

avish_engineer: (typo fix) vish_engineer: are we still saying model-agnostic? some prospects want a Redwood model.
